_about: What stands in each room besides the scenery: pickups, crates, doors and map enemies. The room scene holds the position and the node (its 'placement_id' is the key here); this file holds the contents and the rules, so loot, locks and patrols can change without touching a scene. 'room' is the room id from rooms.json (a test checks the scene really has the node). Opened crates and taken pickups are remembered by id through GameState (mark_opened / is_opened), so they stay taken after a save and load. pickups: item + count and/or credits. crates: items [{item, count}] and/or credits, 'style' is supply (gray Hegemony), chalk (a Coldrunner stash) or wood. doors: to_room + to_spawn; 'requires' is {item, consume, flag}: an item and/or a flag that must be held, 'consume' takes the item the first time; 'locked_message' is what Red reads when it is locked, 'unlocked_message' plays the first time the key works. enemies: enemy is an id in battle/enemies.json (its model and its 'field' speeds), encounter is an id in battle/encounters.json, kind is regular (comes back when you re-enter the room), story or boss (stay beaten: 'defeat_flag' is set on a win), patrol is a list of [x, y, z] offsets from where the enemy stands in the scene. More sections: npcs (a townsperson: speaker id, look, appear_if / hidden, variants by story beat), spots (examine / use spots with variants). Any pickup may carry show_if (a Conditions dictionary) and message_extra (one more line after 'Got X!'); doors may carry width, style (panel / mat / arch) and label. Enemies may also carry: scanner (true = a Signals inspector's hand-scanner cone is his only way to notice Red), hidden (out of the room until a scene shows him), patrol_once (walks the route and stands at its end), walk_speed / chase_speed / linger_s overrides.
